title: Replace OptiSweep End Stop Assembly (End Stops typically work in pairs)
summary: LOTO the OptiSweep tipper, replace the damaged end stop assembly using two new M8x40 socket-head screws with Loctite®, and inspect the opposite end stop for damage (end stops typically work in pairs).
when_to_use: Use when an OptiSweep tipper end stop assembly is damaged and needs replacement, and you must also check the opposite end stop because end stops typically work in pairs.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform physical lockout/tagout (LOTO), remove and replace the end stop assembly, and inspect the opposite end stop for damage.
safety_notes: Perform LOTO of the tipper before removing the side panel (if necessary) and before removing/mounting end stop hardware.
access_or_tools_needed: Replacement parts: End stop; two (2) M8x40 socket-head cap screws (per end stop)
Tools: 3/8-in. wrench or socket, 6-mm hex wrench, Loctite®

system_preconditions: Tipper is available for LOTO (Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure on page 2).
external_references: Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

visual_references.description: Figure 7-12: End Stop diagram showing the end stop assembly and the M8x40 socket-head screws used for mounting (top/bottom end stops).

steps.title: Review the end-stop pairing note and collision implication
steps.purpose: Ensure you inspect the opposite end stop because end stops typically work in pairs.
steps.instruction: Before starting the physical work, apply the pairing logic: a collision at the bottom often indicates a collision at the top; therefore, a damaged bottom end stop suggests one of the top end stops is also damaged (exception: belt failure).
steps.expected_result: You are prepared to inspect the opposite end stop for damage after replacing the damaged one.
steps.healthy_condition: Your plan includes checking the opposite end stop for damage, consistent with the pairing note.
steps.failure_condition: You replace only the damaged end stop without checking the opposite end stop, despite the pairing note.

actions.label: Apply pairing logic
actions.exact_action: Note that the end stops typically work in pairs. In most cases, a collision at the bottom means there is also a collision at the top.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “Note that the end stops typically work in pairs. In most cases, a collision at the bottom means there is also a collision at the top… An exception to this could be in the event of a belt failure.”

steps.title: LOTO the tipper
steps.purpose: Make the tipper safe for mechanical replacement work.
steps.instruction: LOTO the tipper using the “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” procedure on page 2.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is locked out/tagged out per the Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure before you remove hardware.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is in place before side panel removal (if necessary) and before removing the end stop screws.
steps.failure_condition: You attempt to remove the side panel or end stop screws without LOTO.

actions.label: Lockout/Tagout tipper
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “1. LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).”

steps.title: Remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor
steps.purpose: Provide access to the end stop mounting hardware.
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws of the side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (only if necessary) and the motor area is accessible for end stop screw removal.
steps.healthy_condition: Side panel removal is complete and you can reach the end stop mounting screws with the tipper still under LOTO.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot access the end stop mounting screws because the side panel was not removed when needed, or you proceed without maintaining LOTO.

actions.label: Remove side panel
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

stop_or_escalate_if: If access to the motor is not possible without removing the side panel, ensure LOTO is maintained before proceeding.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “2. If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.”

steps.title: Remove the two M8 socket-head screws holding the end stops
steps.purpose: Detach the damaged end stop assembly from the tipper.
steps.instruction: Remove the two (2) M8 socket-head screws holding the end stops in place.
steps.expected_result: The end stop assembly is unfastened and can be removed/replaced.
steps.healthy_condition: Both M8 socket-head screws are removed and the end stop is free from its mounting points.
steps.failure_condition: Only one screw is removed, screws are stripped, or you remove hardware without LOTO.

actions.label: Remove end stop screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the two (2) M8 socket-head screws holding the end stops in place.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “3. Remove the two (2) M8 socket-head screws holding the end stops in place.”

steps.title: Mount the new end stop using two new M8x40 socket-head screws with Loctite®
steps.purpose: Install the replacement end stop assembly securely.
steps.instruction: Mount the new end stop with two (2) new M8 socket-head screws and Loctite®.
steps.expected_result: New end stop is mounted using two new M8 socket-head screws with Loctite®.
steps.healthy_condition: Both mounting screws are installed on the new end stop and Loctite® is used as specified.
steps.failure_condition: Old screws are reused, Loctite® is omitted, or the end stop is not seated at the mounting points.

actions.label: Install replacement end stop
actions.exact_action: Mount the new end stop with two (2) new M8 socket-head screws and Loctite®.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “Required Tools… Replacement Parts: End stop, two (2) M8x40 socket-head cap screws (per end stop)… Tools Needed: 3/8-in. wrench or socket, 6-mm hex wrench, Loctite®”
“4. Mount the new end stop with two (2) new M8 socket-head screws and Loctite®.”

steps.title: Check the opposite end stop for damage and replace if necessary
steps.purpose: Prevent repeat faults by addressing the paired end stop condition.
steps.instruction: Check the opposite end stop for damage and replace it if necessary.
steps.expected_result: Opposite end stop is inspected; if damaged, it is replaced.
steps.healthy_condition: Opposite end stop shows no damage (or is replaced if damage is found).
steps.failure_condition: Opposite end stop is damaged but left unreplaced.

actions.label: Inspect opposite end stop
actions.exact_action: Check the opposite end stop for damage and replace if necessary.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the opposite end stop is found damaged, replace it as well (end stops typically work in pairs).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “5. Check the opposite end stop for damage and replace if necessary.”

steps.title: Reinstall side panels if necessary and restart the operator station
steps.purpose: Restore the station to service after mechanical replacement.
steps.instruction: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary, then re-start the operator station (see “Starting The Operator Station” on page 66).
steps.expected_result: Side panels are reinstalled (if removed) and the operator station is restarted.
steps.healthy_condition: Station is returned to normal configuration and operator station restart is completed per the referenced procedure.
steps.failure_condition: Side panels are not reinstalled after removal, or operator station is not restarted per the referenced procedure.

actions.label: Reinstall side panels
actions.exact_action: Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary.

actions.label: Restart operator station
actions.exact_action: Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “6. Reinstall the top and/or bottom side panels, if necessary. 7. Re-start the operator station (see "Starting The Operator Station" on page 66).”

success_criteria: Damaged end stop is replaced with a new end stop mounted using two new M8 socket-head screws with Loctite®.
Opposite end stop is checked for damage and replaced if necessary.
Side panels are reinstalled (if removed) and the operator station is restarted.
healthy_conditions: New end stop is mounted using two new M8 socket-head screws with Loctite®.
Opposite end stop is not damaged (or has been replaced if damage was found).
failure_conditions: Opposite end stop remains damaged after inspection.
End stop mounting does not use two new screws and Loctite® as specified.
Side panels are left removed after the replacement.
escalation_guidance: If you cannot access the motor without removing the side panel, maintain LOTO before proceeding.
If the opposite end stop is found damaged, replace it as well (end stops typically work in pairs).

screens_or_images.what_to_look_at: End stops (top and bottom) and the M8x40 socket-head cap screws used for mounting; use to identify the end stop assembly location and mounting hardware.

Figure 7-12: End Stop diagram supports identifying the end stop assembly and M8x40 socket-head screws.

missing_details: The source does not specify whether the removed end stop is the top or bottom unit in the replacement step; the procedure relies on checking the opposite end stop after replacement.
